'''Hubertine Rose Éholie''' (23 May 1934 – 11 May 2019) was an Ivorian academic. Specialising in chemistry, she had a long career at the [[University of Abidjan]]. She retired by 2015 and was a critic of the gender gap of women in academia.

== Biography ==
Éholie was born on 23 May 1934, in [[Burkina Faso]], then part of [[French Ivory Coast]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Profiles of African Scientists|date=1990|publisher=African Academy of Sciences|isbn=9789966831040|page=3|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Q6AsAAAAIAAJ|language=en}}</ref> She studied at the [[University of Poitiers]] and earned a higher education certificate in mathematics, physics, and chemistry in 1957, and a certificate of specialized studies in metallurgy, chemistry and physics in 1960.<ref>{{cite book|title=Profiles of African Scientists|date=1990|publisher=African Academy of Sciences|isbn=9789966831040|page=2|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Q6AsAAAAIAAJ|language=en}}</ref> Éholie earned a [[Doctor of Engineering|Doctor of Engineering Science]] degree in 1966 and a [[Habilitation#France|State Doctorate]] in 1971 at the [[University of Abidjan]].<ref name=was/>

Éholie taught at the {{ill|Lycée classique d'Abidjan|fr}} before a career at the University of Abidjan<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lycée Classique Abidjan {{!}} Les Caïmans |url=https://www.lyceeclassiqueabidjan.org/ |access-date=2026-06-13 |website=lycee-classique |language=fr}}</ref>. She began as a teaching assistant before becoming an assistant lecturer and lecturer in the Faculty of the Sciences. She became a senior lecturer, professor and then tenured professor in the Faculty of Sciences and Techniques. She specialized in crystallography, electro-magnetics, glasses, the silver-arsenic-selenium system, semi-conductors and ternary compounds. She was elected a fellow of the [[World Academy of Sciences|Third World Academy of Sciences]] (now known as [[The World Academy of Sciences]], TWAS), Sub-Saharan Africa Region in 1987 and was one of only 88 fellows elected from that region (as of 2017).{{update inline|date=November 2023}}<ref name=was>{{cite web|title=Éholie, Hubertine Rose|url=http://www.twas-rossa.org.za/network/item/1-twas-fellows/31-eholie-hubertine-rose|publisher=World Academy of Sciences|accessdate=23 November 2017|language=en-gb|archive-date=1 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201040706/http://www.twas-rossa.org.za/network/item/1-twas-fellows/31-eholie-hubertine-rose|url-status=dead}}</ref> She had retired by 2015.<ref name=education>{{cite book|last1=Takyi-Amoako|first1=Emefa|title=Education in West Africa|date=2015|publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing|isbn=9781441177858|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KHp6CAAAQBAJ|language=en}}</ref>

Éholie wrote an article in 1988 for a [[Canadian International Development Agency]] and the [[Third World Academy of Sciences]] conference entitled "The role of women in the scientific and technological development of the third world: the case of Cote d'Ivoire".<ref>{{cite book|last1=M|first1=Faruqui A.|last2=A|first2=Hassan M. H.|last3=G|first3=Sandri|title=Role Of Women In The Development Of Science And Technology In The Third World - Proceedings Of The Conference Organized By The Canadian International Development Agency And The Third World Academy Of Sciences|date=1991|publisher=#N/A|isbn=9789814632959|page=206|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YogvDwAAQBAJ|language=en}}</ref> She was a critic of the gender gap of women in academia in the Côte d'Ivoire, particularly in the sciences.<ref name=education/>

Éholie died on 11 May 2019, aged 84, in the Côte d'Ivoire.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fratmat.info/article/90958/10064/deuil-l-ascad-rend-hommage-au-pr-eholie-hubertine|title=Deuil: L'Ascad rend hommage au Pr Eholié Hubertine|trans-title=Mourning: Ascad pays tribute to Professor Eholié Hubertine|date=2019-06-17|publisher=Fratmat.info|access-date=2023-11-21|language=fr}}</ref>
